title: Which reading belongs to the canary?

beats.say: Checkout just sent one request in ten through a new parser flag. The smoke test passed. Follow the latency trace to its newest dot. Which rollout revision does that dot belong to, and when did the metrics tool see it?

Revision seven, at second one hundred. The dot measures the ninety-fifth percentile of response time, two hundred forty milliseconds. About ninety-five requests in a hundred finish within that time. At second one hundred ten the reading is ten seconds old. Our exercise accepts observations up to thirty seconds old. Should the owner continue, hold, or roll back?

Lay the policy bands over the trace. With smoke passing, readings below two hundred milliseconds can continue. The hold band starts at two hundred. Rollback starts at three hundred. Where does our dot land?

Hold the canary at ten percent. One authenticated measurement and a policy comparison settled the advice. Test-time compute is work spent during inference after training. On this request another model call would buy another opinion. On the repair that follows, it can buy a distinct plan worth checking.

Replay the same checkout rollout with just one change. Put the final reading at three hundred milliseconds. The smoke test still passes. The receipt still belongs to revision seven. Does the upper edge belong to hold or rollback?

Recommend rollback. Equality counts at that upper edge. A failed smoke test would also trigger rollback once the evidence qualifies. These thresholds belong to this exercise. The response goes to the release owner. Changing the live deployment needs separate authorization and a fresh revision check.

Keep the three-hundred-millisecond receipt. Advance the clock to second one hundred thirty. The receipt is exactly thirty seconds old and still qualifies. Advance one more second. Would you send that same advice now?

Withhold it and request a fresh measurement. Age must be between zero and thirty seconds inclusive. Check the deployment, revision, canary share, and types as well. The tool now returns a fresh receipt at second one hundred thirty-one. Read its revision. Six. That still cannot establish what revision seven is doing.

Suppose a model writes Hold inside a field called final. Our parser expects final underscore answer. Its verification summary is present. Correcting the field name makes this response parse. It still needs independent evidence. Model effort can tune deliberation. The controller enforces hard limits across calls and keeps the tool records that justify its advice.

title: Can the selector recognize a sound plan?

beats.say: Holding the canary gives us time to investigate the flag. Compare route timings before blaming the parser. Suppose a generator can find a sound repair on thirty percent of attempts. Best-of-five asks it for five complete candidates. If their errors are independent, how often will the set contain a sound plan?

Count the opposite case. All five must miss. Each miss leaves seventy percent of the previous probability mass. After five misses about seventeen percent remains. Take the complement. About eighty-three percent of sets contain a sound plan. Shared prompts can correlate errors, and even independent draws need a selector.

Here are two proposed routes to the database. The learned scorer gives the legacy adapter point nine six and the feature flag point eight two. Each route needs both hops. Find the hop you would test before trusting that ranking.
Read the compatibility record. The API can enter the feature flag. Its link to the legacy adapter is blocked. Both second hops reach the database. Which candidate can you send?

Send B. Only the feature flag route clears both hops. Rank the eligible plans. Voting on comparable answers is another selector, called self-consistency. Three votes for A would still choose the broken route. Turning up sampling temperature can change the mix of votes without fixing that link.

title: Which partial repair gets another call?

beats.say: Suppose the compatibility check now needs a package plan. A width-two beam keeps up to two unfinished alternatives after each expansion. The nightly parser requires a newer runtime. Which pins can still lead to a repair? A pin by itself leaves the job unfinished.

Keep version two and version one. Expand each pin. Version two can add a compatibility shim or call a removed API. Version one can patch the sanitizer or defer its required fix. The score floor is point three five. Which leaf clears that floor but still has to go?

Drop the deferred fix. Its point three nine clears the score floor and leaves the advisory unresolved. The removed API fails too. Save the two completed repairs separately from the frontier. The patch scores point nine six and wins over the shim. With only one level of search we would have no completed plan to return.

A token beam can keep near-identical wordings. Here the alternatives are distinct package choices. To revisit feasible branches, a tree controller can use PUCT. Give each branch its mean outcome plus an exploration bonus. Multiply its prior by the square root of parent visits, then divide by one plus child visits. Here the exploration constant is one. Which branch gets the next visit?

Visit A. Both means are one half. A adds point four and B adds point three. Suppose A now returns one. Update its mean to three quarters, count its second visit, and increment the parent to seventeen. A stays ahead. A visit changes the evidence for the next allocation. A high visit score alone cannot release a repair.

title: Where can a checker save a generator call?

beats.say: Follow the version-two branch one call at a time. Parse the manifest. Pin the parser. Request the API step. One controller inspects only finished outcomes. The other checks each step against the installed runtime. If the API was removed, which controller still pays for a fourth call?

The outcome-only controller requests call four. The stepwise controller stops at three when compatibility fails. A learned process evaluator can suggest a similar stop where an exact check is unavailable. Its training labels describe individual steps. An outcome evaluator learns from labels on whole solutions.

Check the checker too. A quoted false is text. A missing or nonfinite score must take a failure path before ranking. A low process score can prune a valid plan. Compare saved generator calls with the cost of verification and false rejection on held-out repairs.

Try grading this solution. It divides by x to solve x times the quantity x minus one equals zero. That division loses the possible root zero. The author happens to list both correct roots at the end. If the grader accepts the work, which error should you count?

Count a false acceptance. Six accepts among eight deliberately flawed solutions give seventy-five percent false acceptance. A solver that answers nine of ten ordinary problems correctly has ninety percent accuracy on a different set.

A verifier can also supply a training reward. Give four repairs the same test. Two pass and earn one apiece. Two fail and earn zero. The group mean is one half. A group-relative update favors the above-average repairs. Once the weights are frozen, each new release still needs its own evidence.

This request has four thousand generated tokens. Each socket holds one hundred. Calls B and A each reserve fifteen hundred before they start. C asks for fifteen hundred too. Trace its outline against the empty sockets. Can it start?

C waits. Only a thousand tokens are free. A finishes early. Its receipt says nine hundred used. Keep those nine sockets charged and release the six beside them. B is still running. How large is the opening now?

Sixteen hundred tokens are free. Admit C for fifteen hundred. Its reservation uses the six sockets A released and nine of the ten that were already empty. One hundred stays free. Generator, verifier, and retry calls all draw from this same request.

A retry delivers A's receipt again. Match the call ID and usage. Nine hundred has already been charged, so the balances stay put. A conflicting receipt or usage above a reservation requires reconciliation. Serialize admission so two workers cannot claim the same opening.

Now B times out. We still lack its usage receipt. Keep B's fifteen hundred reserved. A deadline closes dispatch and can trigger cancellation. Only settled usage or confirmed unused capacity can free that space. Time, input charges, and device memory each need their own limit.

title: How much memory do the branches share?

beats.say: The serving engine also needs space for keys and values. In this uniform full-attention model, multiply two by eighty layers, eight key-value heads, one hundred twenty-eight values per head, and two bytes per value. That gives three hundred twenty kibibytes for one live token.

Each row here holds sixteen thousand three hundred eighty-four tokens. The first three blocks match across all eight rows. Each last block belongs to a different branch. At five gibibytes per row, separate allocations occupy forty gibibytes. Count the blocks we actually need if those stems can share storage.

Keep one stem and eight tails. Each block holds four thousand ninety-six tokens. Eleven blocks occupy thirteen and three quarters gibibytes before overhead. Sharing needs identical token IDs and positions, compatible model, adapter and cache settings, and the same authorized scope. Real allocators also pay for rounding and fragmentation.

Zoom in on one shared page. Four branches reference it and a device reader is still active. Two branches prune. The reader finishes. Look at the two remaining references. Can the allocator give this page to another request?

Wait for both remaining references to leave. Now reclaim the page. A writer can copy a shared page before changing it. Discarding a still-needed value to save space can damage a later answer. Recurrent depth spends computation inside a purpose-built model and requires a different architecture.

title: What can the owner receive at the deadline?

beats.say: The router can finish a verified threshold lookup immediately. A missing observation calls for a tool or authorized review. A repair with testable alternatives can justify search. On this repair the earlier best score was point seven two. The last three were point seven zero, point seven one, and point six nine. Would one more expansion qualify under a rule that requires improvement?

Stop this branch. Its recent maximum, point seven one, falls below the earlier best. This plateau rule can lose a future gain. Tune it on held-out repairs. Stop repeated states as well, and enforce hard time, depth and token limits even when the proxy keeps rising.

Return to checkout. Two drafts share a release queue. C has finished and its hold recommendation has passed every evidence check. F has a higher proxy score. Its revision check is still running. Watch the deadline approach. Which draft can go back if that check has not finished?

Time is up. Freeze the review exactly here. F has only two of its three checks. C has completed all three, its text contains an answer, and the revision-seven observation is still fresh. Which advisory goes to the owner?

Return C. A higher score cannot finish F's check. An empty or whitespace-only completed draft also fails the release gate. If no completed answer has usable text and independent evidence, abstain. The owner can see that the metrics check completed. The adapter keeps unfinished reasoning and uncalibrated scores out of that progress stream.

Try this on four held-out incidents. Freeze the observations and policy for each, and split by incident so paraphrases cannot leak across sets. Compare single path and best-of-three at matched total generator plus verifier cost. In this small example, which incident gains a correct recommendation, and where does extra search hurt?

The repair gains a correct plan. On stale evidence the second controller gives unsafe advice where the first abstained. At the boundary it also abstains where one path gave the right advice. Both return two correct recommendations. Report correctness, unsafe advice, and abstentions separately. Measure elapsed time and all call costs. Increase the budget only on a workload where the measured gain earns it.

Now read one request trace from left to right. The gateway acknowledges it at a tenth of a second. The first model token arrives at eight tenths. The checked advisory goes out at three seconds. A quick status update can hide a slow final answer. An extra revision can even spoil a sound recommendation. Compare the whole trace at the same total cost.

One final dispatch decision. In a new six-thousand-token request, C spent nine hundred on a completed hold advisory. A and B each reserved two thousand. D wants fifteen hundred. A now reports fourteen hundred used. Does D fit, and how much capacity will remain?

Settle A. Its unused six hundred takes free capacity from eleven hundred to seventeen hundred. Admit D for fifteen hundred. Two hundred tokens remain free. At the deadline, second one hundred thirty, C's revision-seven reading from second one hundred qualifies at the thirty-second edge. Return C. B and D still hold thirty-five hundred tokens between them.

Replay the deadline. Change just the observation time to second ninety-nine. Keep the same revision, passing smoke test, two hundred forty milliseconds, and the same unfinished calls. Should C go back, and how much capacity must you still reserve?

Abstain and ask for a fresh latency measurement. The receipt is thirty-one seconds old. The deadline leaves no time to refresh it. B and D still hold thirty-five hundred tokens until their usage is known. The reply can close while the ledger stays open for those receipts.
